title: An Ideal Student Paragraph
excerpt: An ideal student treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. Such a learner attends classes regularly, listens carefully, asks questions, and reviews lessons before they are forgotten.
plainContent: Habits that make learning meaningful An ideal student treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. Such a learner attends classes regularly, listens carefully, asks questions, and reviews lessons before they are forgotten. Instead of memorising every sentence, the student tries to understand ideas and explain them independently. Good study is balanced with good character. An ideal student respects parents, teachers, classmates, and school rules. The student is truthful, punctual, helpful, and willing to admit mistakes. Exercise, sleep, and recreation are also important because a healthy body supports concentration. An excellent learner does not become proud after success or discouraged after failure. He or she helps weaker classmates, keeps notes organised, avoids wasting time, and uses technology responsibly. These habits prepare a person not only for examinations but also for useful citizenship. True excellence combines knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving.

title: Tree Plantation paragraph
excerpt: Tree plantation means deliberately growing trees in suitable places and caring for them. It is important in Bangladesh because trees provide oxygen, shade, fruit, wood, soil protection, and habitats for birds and other animals.
plainContent: Tree Plantation Tree plantation means deliberately growing trees in suitable places and caring for them. It is important in Bangladesh because trees provide oxygen, shade, fruit, wood, soil protection, and habitats for birds and other animals. Their roots help reduce erosion, while leaves cool the surroundings and improve air quality. We can plant trees beside roads, around schools, near ponds, on unused land, and in home gardens. Fruit trees can provide food and income, while native shade trees benefit people and wildlife. A planting programme should select healthy saplings, prepare the soil, water them regularly, and protect them from grazing animals. Planting without later care often leads to failure. People should stop unnecessary cutting and replace trees that must be removed. Schools and local groups can observe a tree-planting day, but caring for the saplings throughout the year is more important than a ceremony. By increasing green spaces and protecting old trees, we help the climate, soil, economy, and health of our communities. Every household and institution can contribute.

title: A School Magazine paragraph
excerpt: A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by students and teachers. It may appear once a year and include poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews, and records of important school events.
plainContent: A publication made by a school community A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by students and teachers. It may appear once a year and include poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews, and records of important school events. A teacher usually guides the editorial committee, while students collect submissions, edit drafts, arrange illustrations, and check proofs. The process teaches planning, cooperation, careful reading, and respect for other people’s ideas. A student who is quiet in class may discover confidence after seeing a poem or report printed in the magazine. The publication also preserves the character of the school during a particular year. Readers can learn about achievements, clubs, celebrations, and community projects. A magazine should welcome different abilities rather than publish only perfect writing. With encouragement and honest editing, it becomes both a record of school life and a training ground for future communicators.

title: A Winter Morning paragraph
excerpt: A winter morning arrives slowly under a veil of mist. Before sunrise, trees and rooftops look blurred, and the familiar road seems shorter because the fog hides its far end.
plainContent: A quiet morning in the cold season A winter morning arrives slowly under a veil of mist. Before sunrise, trees and rooftops look blurred, and the familiar road seems shorter because the fog hides its far end. The air feels sharp, so people wrap themselves in shawls, sweaters, or blankets. The scene changes when the sun rises. Golden light gradually burns away the mist, dew shines on grass, and birds begin to call from the branches. Farmers lead their cattle to the fields, while children hurry to school after warming themselves beside a small fire. Tea stalls become popular because a hot cup gives workers comfort before the day begins. Winter mornings are especially pleasant to those who can enjoy them at leisure. Date juice, cakes, fresh vegetables, and warm sunshine are seasonal pleasures. Yet poor people often suffer because they lack warm clothing and shelter. We should share blankets and food with neighbours who need help. A winter morning combines beauty, freshness, and hardship. Its peaceful atmosphere is memorable, but its human lesson is equally important: comfort should not make us forget the vulnerable.

title: Load Shedding Paragraph
excerpt: Load shedding is the planned interruption of electricity when demand is greater than the available supply or when the power network needs protection. It may also occur because of fuel shortages, damaged equipment, storms, or faults in transmission lines.
plainContent: Load Shedding Load shedding is the planned interruption of electricity when demand is greater than the available supply or when the power network needs protection. It may also occur because of fuel shortages, damaged equipment, storms, or faults in transmission lines. An unexpected power cut disturbs homes, schools, hospitals, shops, factories, and farms. Students cannot study comfortably, food may spoil in a refrigerator, water pumps may stop, and businesses can lose working hours. Hospitals need generators and careful planning because many patients depend on electrical equipment. Repeated cuts can also damage appliances when the current returns suddenly. The problem can be reduced by producing sufficient electricity, repairing the grid, preventing illegal connections, and using renewable sources such as solar power. Consumers should switch off unnecessary lights and fans, use energy-efficient appliances, and avoid wasting electricity during peak periods. Authorities should publish reliable schedules and give priority to essential services. Responsible use by citizens, combined with investment in generation and distribution, can make the supply more dependable.

title: How to Write an Application: Format and Examples
excerpt: First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing. Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation.
plainContent: Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department head, or another authority for different reasons. For example, you may need to write an application for leave, a testimonial, a transfer certificate, permission for a study tour, or another school or college matter. University students and job seekers also write formal applications for academic and professional purposes. The good news is that most formal applications follow a simple structure. Once you understand the format, you can write an application for almost any situation. This guide explains the basic application writing format and provides examples for school, college, university, and job applications. What Is an Application? An application is a formal written request made to a person or authority. For example: A student writes to the headmaster for leave. A student writes to the principal for a testimonial. A university student writes to the examination office for a transcript. A student writes to an authority for permission to join a study tour. A job seeker writes to an employer to apply for a position. The purpose of an application should be clear from the beginning. Avoid unnecessary information and explain exactly what you are requesting. Basic Application Writing Format A formal application usually contains these parts: Date Name and designation of the recipient Institution or organisation Address Subject Salutation Main body Closing Name and identifying information of the applicant A simple structure looks like this: Date The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address] Subject: Application for [purpose]. Sir/Madam, First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing. Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation. Final paragraph: Clearly state what you are requesting. Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/ID] The exact format can vary between institutions, so students should follow any specific instructions given by their school, college, university, or employer. 1. Application for Leave A leave application is written when you need permission to remain absent from school, college, or another institution. Example: Leave Application for Illness 15 January 2026 The Headmaster Ideal High School Motijheel, Dhaka Subject: Application for leave of absence. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class IX, Section B, of your school. I have been suffering from a high fever for the last three days, and the doctor has advised me to take rest. For this reason, I will not be able to attend school from 15 January to 18 January 2026. I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for these four days. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Md. Rakib Hasan Class IX, Section B Roll No. 17 What to include in a leave application Make sure you mention: The reason for your absence The dates of your leave Your class or department Your roll or student ID Any supporting document if the institution requires one Do not write a long explanation. Give only the information the authority needs. 2. Application for a Testimonial A testimonial is an official document that may provide information about a student's academic record, conduct, or period of study at an institution. Students may need a testimonial after completing SSC or HSC or when applying for further education or other purposes. Example: Testimonial Application 10 February 2026 The Principal Dhaka College New Market, Dhaka Subject: Application for a testimonial. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I passed the HSC examination in 2025 from your college under the Dhaka Education Board. I am now preparing to apply for higher studies and require a testimonial from the college. I therefore request you to kindly issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Sumaiya Akter HSC 2025, Science Group Roll No. 124356 Tip for students If the institution has a specific testimonial form, use that form instead of writing a separate application. Some Bangladeshi institutions provide their own testimonial forms with fields for student information and academic details. 3. Application for an Academic Transcript University students may need an academic transcript when applying for higher studies, scholarships, employment, or other official purposes. The procedure is different from one university to another. Some universities require a specific form, fee payment, clearance, or supporting documents. Example 22 March 2026 The Controller of Examinations University of Dhaka Dhaka-1000 Subject: Application for issuance of academic transcript. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Engineering from your university in 2025. I now require

title: Air Pollution Paragraph
excerpt: Air pollution occurs when smoke, dust, poisonous gases, or tiny particles enter the atmosphere in harmful amounts. Vehicle exhaust, brick kilns, factories, burning rubbish, construction work, and forest fires are common sources.
plainContent: When the air becomes unsafe Air pollution occurs when smoke, dust, poisonous gases, or tiny particles enter the atmosphere in harmful amounts. Vehicle exhaust, brick kilns, factories, burning rubbish, construction work, and forest fires are common sources. In crowded cities, pollution can become especially serious when wind is weak. Breathing polluted air may irritate the eyes and throat and can worsen asthma, heart disease, and other respiratory problems. Children, older people, and outdoor workers are often most vulnerable. Pollution also damages crops, buildings, animals, and the climate. The solution requires both public policy and personal responsibility. Authorities can enforce emission standards, improve public transport, control construction dust, and promote clean energy. Citizens can avoid burning waste, maintain vehicles, plant suitable trees, and walk or share transport when possible. Schools can teach children to notice local pollution and support clean-air campaigns. Protecting the atmosphere is a shared duty because everyone depends on healthy air.

title: My Hobby Paragraph
excerpt: Gardening is my favourite hobby. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home.
plainContent: My Hobby Gardening is my favourite hobby. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care. Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food. I reuse kitchen containers as planters and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with neighbors. This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility.

title: Early Rising paragraph
excerpt: Early rising means waking at a regular time that allows a person to begin the day without haste. The quiet hours can be used for prayer, exercise, reading, revision, or planning.
plainContent: Beginning the day with purpose Early rising means waking at a regular time that allows a person to begin the day without haste. The quiet hours can be used for prayer, exercise, reading, revision, or planning. Fresh air and fewer distractions often make the morning feel especially productive. The habit is helpful only when it follows adequate sleep. A student who stays awake late and wakes before resting properly will be tired, not successful. A fixed bedtime, limited screen use at night, and preparation of school materials can make morning rising easier. People have different routines, so no single clock time suits everyone. What matters is a balanced schedule that includes sleep, study, work, meals, and recreation. A calm beginning can improve punctuality and concentration, but health should never be sacrificed merely to claim that one rises early.

title: Deforestation Paragraph
excerpt: Trees are being removed for fuel, timber, roads, farms, and construction. When this clearing continues without replanting, the result is deforestation.
plainContent: The consequences of cutting forests Trees are being removed for fuel, timber, roads, farms, and construction. When this clearing continues without replanting, the result is deforestation. It destroys animal habitats, weakens soil, reduces rainfall absorption, and adds to global warming because fewer trees remain to take in carbon dioxide. Deforested land is more likely to suffer erosion, floods, drought, and extreme heat. People who depend on forests for food, medicine, or work also lose important resources. The damage can continue for many years after the last tree is cut. We should protect natural forests, enforce laws against illegal logging, and restore damaged land with suitable species. Schools and families can plant and care for trees, reduce wasteful paper use, and teach others why forests matter. Conservation is a shared duty because healthy forests support a healthy society.

title: Eve Teasing Paragraph
excerpt: “Eve-teasing” is a common term for unwanted comments, gestures, following, staring, or other harassment directed at girls and women. It is not harmless fun.
plainContent: Ending harassment in public spaces “Eve-teasing” is a common term for unwanted comments, gestures, following, staring, or other harassment directed at girls and women. It is not harmless fun. It creates fear, restricts movement, interrupts education, and denies a person the right to travel safely. Families and schools should teach respect, equality, consent, and responsible conduct from an early age. Witnesses can support the victim, seek help from trusted adults or authorities, and avoid blaming the person who was harassed. Communities need safe transport, lighting, complaint systems, and prompt enforcement of the law. A girl should never be told to change her education, clothing, or dreams to accommodate someone else’s misconduct. Boys and men must understand that silence and peer approval can encourage abuse. Public spaces become safer when every person rejects harassment and protects the dignity of others.

title: Physical Exercise Paragraph
excerpt: Physical exercise is the movement of the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, swimming, cycling, running, gardening, games, and sports can all keep us active.
plainContent: Physical Exercise Physical exercise is the movement of the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, swimming, cycling, running, gardening, games, and sports can all keep us active. Exercise makes muscles stronger, improves blood circulation, supports a healthy weight, and helps the mind remain fresh. A young and fit person may choose a sport or a brisk run, while an elderly or weak person can begin with gentle walking and stretching. No single activity is suitable for everyone. It is wise to warm up, practise regularly, drink water, and stop if the body feels unwell. Good food and sufficient sleep are also necessary for health. Exercise teaches discipline as well as fitness. A student who takes a short walk or plays outdoors often returns to study with better concentration. Many activities are free, so lack of money need not prevent a healthy routine. We should avoid sitting for long hours and make movement part of everyday life. Good health supports work, study, and happiness, making physical exercise an important habit for people of every age.

title: Gender Discrimination Paragraph
excerpt: Gender discrimination occurs when people are treated differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life.
plainContent: Gender Discrimination Gender discrimination occurs when people are treated differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life. For example, a girl may be discouraged from studying, while a boy may be excused from household duties. Such attitudes prevent families and nations from using the abilities of all their citizens. Everyone deserves equal respect, education, safety, and a fair chance to work. Parents should give sons and daughters the same encouragement, and schools should challenge unfair stereotypes. Laws can protect equal rights, but lasting change also depends on everyday behavior. When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress.

title: Facebook Paragraph for Class 6,7,8,9,10, HSC
excerpt: Facebook is a social networking service where people can communicate, share photographs, join groups, follow news, and promote work or business. It helps relatives and friends remain connected across distance and can support learning or community campaigns.
plainContent: Using Facebook responsibly Facebook is a social networking service where people can communicate, share photographs, join groups, follow news, and promote work or business. It helps relatives and friends remain connected across distance and can support learning or community campaigns. The platform also carries risks. False news can spread quickly, personal details may be misused, and excessive scrolling can consume time needed for study, sleep, or family. Arguments, scams, bullying, and unauthorized sharing of photographs are further dangers. Users should choose strong privacy settings, accept requests carefully, verify important claims before sharing, and use respectful language. They should report harassment, avoid suspicious links, and ask permission before posting another person’s image. Setting a time limit helps keep online activity balanced. Social media is useful when it serves communication and learning. It becomes harmful when it replaces judgement, privacy, or real relationships.

title: Climate Change Paragraph
excerpt: The climate is changing because large amounts of heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories, power stations, and the destruction of forests all contribute to this increase.
plainContent: A changing climate and our responsibility The climate is changing because large amounts of heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories, power stations, and the destruction of forests all contribute to this increase. A warmer planet can bring irregular rain, longer heat waves, melting ice, stronger storms, and rising sea levels. These effects are serious for Bangladesh. Floods and cyclones can damage homes and crops, while salt water may enter fields and drinking-water sources. Poor families usually suffer most because they have fewer resources to rebuild. We cannot solve the problem through one action. Public authorities should protect forests, develop clean energy, improve warning systems, and plan climate-resilient towns. Citizens can conserve electricity, plant and protect trees, reduce waste, and use buses or bicycles when practical. Education is important because informed people make better choices. Climate change is not a distant issue. Careful decisions today can reduce future damage and protect the lives and livelihoods of coming generations.

title: Price Hike Paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC,HSC
excerpt: A price hike is a sustained increase in the cost of everyday goods and services. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent, or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more for the same standard of living.
plainContent: Price Hike A price hike is a sustained increase in the cost of everyday goods and services. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent, or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more for the same standard of living. The burden is especially heavy for workers whose salaries do not rise with the market. Prices may increase because of inflation, higher fuel and production costs, floods or other disasters, shortages, currency changes, transport problems, hoarding, and excessive profit-taking. A disruption in one part of the supply chain can affect the final price in a shop. The result can be anxiety, reduced nutrition, postponed treatment, and greater poverty. The government can respond by ensuring adequate supply, improving storage and transport, monitoring markets, taking action against illegal hoarding, and assisting families in genuine difficulty. Farmers and small traders also need fair access to finance and markets. Consumers should compare prices, avoid waste, and not create artificial shortages by panic buying. A coordinated effort can protect both producers and buyers while the economy stabilises.

title: Dhaka Metro Rail paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: Metro rail is a rapid urban transport system in which electric trains travel along dedicated tracks, often above busy roads or underground. It can carry large numbers of passengers quickly and reduce pressure on crowded streets.
plainContent: Metro Rail Metro rail is a rapid urban transport system in which electric trains travel along dedicated tracks, often above busy roads or underground. It can carry large numbers of passengers quickly and reduce pressure on crowded streets. In a growing city, a dependable metro service saves commuting time, lowers fuel use, and can reduce air pollution and traffic noise. Passengers should queue, buy the correct ticket, keep stations clean, and offer priority seats to those who need them. Safety rules must be followed near platforms and doors. Metro rail alone cannot solve every transport problem; buses, walking routes, cycling facilities, and good planning are also necessary. With responsible use and careful expansion, it can make urban travel cleaner and more efficient.

title: International Mother Language Day paragraph
excerpt: International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honor the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla.
plainContent: International Mother Language Day International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honor the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla. Several demonstrators lost their lives, and their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights. People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programs, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding.

title: A Lion and a Mouse Completing Story for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: A lion was sleeping beneath a tree when a mouse ran across his paw. The lion caught the little creature and prepared to punish it.
plainContent: Small help, great value A lion was sleeping beneath a tree when a mouse ran across his paw. The lion caught the little creature and prepared to punish it. The mouse begged for freedom and promised that it might help him someday. The lion laughed at the unlikely idea but released it. Some time later, hunters trapped the lion in a strong net. His loud roars reached the mouse, which hurried to the place. Using its sharp teeth, it gnawed through the ropes one strand at a time. Soon the lion was free, and he understood that size does not determine usefulness. The lion thanked the mouse and changed his view of weaker creatures. Everyone has abilities that may become valuable in an unexpected situation. Kindness also creates bonds that return when help is needed. Moral: Never despise a small friend; kindness is rarely wasted.

title: Letter How to improve English
excerpt: You can improve English through small, regular habits. Read a short article or story daily and note useful expressions rather than isolated words.
plainContent: Letter: Ways to Improve English Dear Tuhin, You can improve English through small, regular habits. Read a short article or story daily and note useful expressions rather than isolated words. Listen to clear conversations, repeat sentences aloud, and practice speaking with a friend. Write a diary entry or a short paragraph each day, then check the grammar and spelling. Keep a personal vocabulary notebook and use new words in your own sentences. Do not be embarrassed by mistakes; correction is part of learning. A dictionary and reliable learning website can answer questions, but real practice is essential. With patience and steady effort, your reading, writing, listening, and speaking will all become stronger. With love, Mim

title: Letter about Brilliant Success
excerpt: I was delighted to hear that you achieved an excellent result in the SSC examination. Please accept my warm congratulations.
plainContent: Letter: Congratulations on Brilliant Success Dear Tanvir, I was delighted to hear that you achieved an excellent result in the SSC examination. Please accept my warm congratulations. Your success is the reward for your regular study, careful preparation, and determination. It has also brought pride and happiness to your parents and teachers. Do not become careless after this achievement. Continue learning with the same discipline, and choose your next course thoughtfully. I am sure that your honesty and hard work will help you reach an even brighter goal. With best wishes, Rahim

title: Letter about Preparation for Exam
excerpt: You asked about my examination preparation. I made a timetable that divides each day into short study sessions and includes sleep, meals, and exercise.
plainContent: Letter: How I Am Preparing for the Examination Dear Shila, You asked about my examination preparation. I made a timetable that divides each day into short study sessions and includes sleep, meals, and exercise. I am reviewing difficult chapters first, practicing questions under time limits, and keeping a notebook of mistakes. I also discuss confusing topics with my teachers instead of memorizing blindly. Each week I revise earlier lessons so that they do not fade. I am trying to remain calm and avoid wasting time on my phone. Your advice to study consistently has been very helpful. Yours affectionately, Mitu

title: A Street Hawker paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: A street hawker sells goods from a basket, cart, or temporary stand instead of a permanent shop. Hawkers may offer fruit, vegetables, snacks, clothes, toys, household items, or newspapers.
plainContent: Small trade along the roadside A street hawker sells goods from a basket, cart, or temporary stand instead of a permanent shop. Hawkers may offer fruit, vegetables, snacks, clothes, toys, household items, or newspapers. Their flexible prices and convenient locations make them useful to busy customers, especially in crowded neighbourhoods. Most hawkers work long hours in sun and rain and have little protection from eviction, illness, or loss of stock. Food sellers also face the responsibility of keeping products covered and using clean water. Unplanned stalls can narrow pavements and create waste, so fair rules are needed. Municipal authorities can provide designated vending spaces, waste bins, and hygiene guidance while protecting pedestrian paths. Customers should bargain fairly, avoid littering, and choose safe food. Street hawkers contribute to the local economy, and orderly planning can support both their livelihood and the public’s right to move safely.

title: The Life of a Farmer paragraph
excerpt: A farmer grows crops and raises animals that help feed society. In Bangladesh many farmers cultivate rice, wheat, pulses, vegetables, jute, sugarcane, and other produce.
plainContent: The Life of a Farmer A farmer grows crops and raises animals that help feed society. In Bangladesh many farmers cultivate rice, wheat, pulses, vegetables, jute, sugarcane, and other produce. Their work begins early, when they prepare soil, sow seeds, manage water, remove weeds, and protect plants from pests. Farming demands patience and physical effort. A farmer may work under strong sun or heavy rain and wait months before knowing whether the harvest will succeed. Floods, drought, cyclones, disease, and insects can destroy crops. When the harvest is good, the farmer supplies food to markets and earns money for the family; when it fails, debt and hardship may follow. Farmers need fair prices, quality seed, affordable credit, irrigation, storage, crop insurance, and access to agricultural advice. Better roads and markets can reduce waste between field and consumer. Respecting farmers also means avoiding food waste and understanding the labour behind every meal. Their contribution is fundamental to national life, so agriculture deserves sustained public support and modern, climate-resilient methods.

title: My Village Paragraph for Class 5,6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: A village is a quiet community where people live close to fields, ponds, trees, and one another. My village, Barachapa, lies in Monohardi Upazila of Narsingdi.
plainContent: My Village A village is a quiet community where people live close to fields, ponds, trees, and one another. My village, Barachapa, lies in Monohardi Upazila of Narsingdi. It is not a large place, yet its green landscape and friendly people make it special to me. About eight thousand residents live here. Farmers form the largest group, while teachers, shopkeepers, office workers, fishers, and other professionals also contribute to village life. Muslims and Hindus live together respectfully and share one another’s joys and difficulties. The village has primary and secondary schools, madrasahs, a market, a health centre, a post office, and places of worship. A paved road joins it to the main highway, and smaller roads connect the neighbourhoods. The fields become bright with crops during the growing season. Fresh vegetables, fish, milk, and clean air are among the benefits of rural life. A canal, shady trees, gardens, and open sky add to the scenery. Although modern facilities are increasing, the village still retains its calm character. I love my village because it is beautiful, cooperative, and closely connected to nature. I hope to help its people prosper while preserving its peaceful environment.

title: Importance of games and sports Dialogue
excerpt: A Conversation About Games and Sports: Siam opens the conversation by asking, “I spend all my free time studying. Is playing really necessary?” Tania responds, “Yes. Appropriate games and sports strengthen the body and refresh the mind.”
plainContent: A Conversation About Games and Sports Siam: I spend all my free time studying. Is playing really necessary? Tania: Yes. Appropriate games and sports strengthen the body and refresh the mind. Siam: Do they help with schoolwork too? Tania: Regular activity can improve concentration, discipline, teamwork, and confidence. Team games also teach us to follow rules and accept both victory and defeat. Siam: Some students play for hours and neglect their lessons. Tania: Balance is important. A timetable can give time to study, sleep, exercise, and recreation. Safe facilities and fair play matter as well. Siam: I will join the school practice for a reasonable period each afternoon. Tania: Good choice. A healthy student needs both a trained mind and an active body.

title: Morning Walk Dialogue for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: A Conversation About a Morning Walk: Rony opens the conversation by asking, “You look energetic today. Did you exercise?” Lima responds, “I took a brisk walk before breakfast. The cool air made it easy to continue.”
plainContent: A Conversation About a Morning Walk Rony: You look energetic today. Did you exercise? Lima: I took a brisk walk before breakfast. The cool air made it easy to continue. Rony: What benefits do you notice? Lima: Walking improves fitness, supports the heart, refreshes the mind, and helps me begin my studies with concentration. Rony: Do we need special equipment? Lima: Comfortable shoes and a safe route are enough. We should start gently, keep a steady pace, and drink water. Rony: I usually wake late and feel tired all day. Lima: Try going to bed on time and walking for twenty minutes at first. Rony: I will join you tomorrow, provided we choose a safe road away from traffic.

title: Proper Use of Time dialogue
excerpt: A Dialogue on Using Time Properly: Sajib opens the conversation by asking, “You seem relaxed before the examination. Have you finished your revision?” Nayeem responds, “I made a timetable last month and followed it most days.
plainContent: A Dialogue on Using Time Properly Sajib: You seem relaxed before the examination. Have you finished your revision? Nayeem: I made a timetable last month and followed it most days. I divide large chapters into small tasks. Sajib: I often lose an hour to my phone and then try to study late at night. Nayeem: A schedule helps. Keep the phone away during study periods and set a clear stopping time. Short breaks make the work easier. Sajib: Do you study all day? Nayeem: No. I leave time for sleep, meals, exercise, prayer, and family. Using time well means giving each duty its proper place, not remaining busy every minute. Sajib: What if an unexpected task appears? Nayeem: I keep some free space in the plan and complete the most important work first. At night I check what was done and adjust tomorrow’s list. Sajib: I understand. Time cannot be stored for later. Nayeem: Exactly. Once a day passes, we can only learn from it. Good habits turn small periods into steady progress.

title: Importance of Learning English paragraph
excerpt: English is an international language used in education, science, business, travel, technology, and communication. A student who develops English skills can read a wider range of books, follow online lessons, apply for scholarships, and communicate with people…
plainContent: The Importance of Learning English English is an international language used in education, science, business, travel, technology, and communication. A student who develops English skills can read a wider range of books, follow online lessons, apply for scholarships, and communicate with people from many countries. It is also useful for higher study and many careers. Learning a language takes regular practice rather than memorizing a few difficult words. Students should read simple texts, listen carefully, speak without fear, and write a little every day. Mistakes are a natural part of improvement. English should not replace the mother tongue; it should add another useful means of expression. With patience and meaningful practice, learners can use English confidently while respecting their own language and culture.

title: A Book Fair Paragraph for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: A book fair is a temporary marketplace where publishers, booksellers, writers, and readers meet. Rows of colourful stalls display storybooks, novels, science books, biographies, dictionaries, and works by local authors.
plainContent: A lively meeting place for readers A book fair is a temporary marketplace where publishers, booksellers, writers, and readers meet. Rows of colourful stalls display storybooks, novels, science books, biographies, dictionaries, and works by local authors. Visitors can examine new publications, compare prices, and often meet writers at discussions or signing sessions. The event is enjoyable, but its greatest value is educational. It introduces children to many kinds of reading and encourages families to make books part of everyday life. Publishers also use the fair to present new ideas and support young writers. A fair may include lectures, quizzes, exhibitions, and cultural programmes as well. When I visit one, I make a list before entering so that excitement does not make me waste money. I choose a few useful books and spend time reading the displays. A well-organised book fair therefore combines recreation with learning and helps build a thoughtful, informed community.

title: The Ant and the Grasshopper Completing Story
excerpt: Throughout the warm months, an ant carried grains to a dry store beneath a tree. Nearby, a grasshopper spent the days singing and resting in the sun.
plainContent: The Ant and the Grasshopper Throughout the warm months, an ant carried grains to a dry store beneath a tree. Nearby, a grasshopper spent the days singing and resting in the sun. The ant invited him to gather food before winter, but the grasshopper replied that there was plenty of time. The ant continued working a little every day. He did not refuse rest or happiness; he simply prepared before the weather changed. Soon cold rain covered the fields, insects disappeared, and the grasshopper found nothing to eat. Hungry and shivering, he went to the ant’s shelter and asked for help. The ant shared a small meal but explained that kindness could not replace planning. He advised the grasshopper to gather food whenever spring returned and to balance enjoyment with responsibility. The grasshopper understood that he had confused leisure with a life without duties. When warm weather came again, he worked beside the ant each morning and sang only after storing enough food. The two friends remained helpful to one another. Moral: Prepare during good times, and do not sacrifice necessary work for immediate pleasure.

title: Padma Bridge paragraph for Class 6,7,8,SSC,HSC
excerpt: The Padma Multipurpose Bridge is one of Bangladesh’s most important transport projects. It crosses the broad Padma River and links Louhajong in Munshiganj with areas of Shariatpur and Madaripur.
plainContent: Padma Bridge The Padma Multipurpose Bridge is one of Bangladesh’s most important transport projects. It crosses the broad Padma River and links Louhajong in Munshiganj with areas of Shariatpur and Madaripur. In this way it gives the southwest a direct connection with Dhaka and the northern and eastern parts of the country. Construction began in 2014, and the bridge was opened by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on 25 June 2022. It is about 6.15 kilometres long and has two levels: the upper deck carries a four-lane road, while the lower deck is designed for a single railway track. Forty-two piers support forty-one steel spans. The project was financed from Bangladesh’s own public resources and built by China Major Bridge Engineering Company. The bridge has reduced dependence on ferries and made travel more predictable. Farmers can send products to markets more quickly, businesses can move goods efficiently, and people in the connected districts can reach hospitals, schools, and workplaces with greater ease. Its value is not only structural; it represents engineering confidence and a long-term investment in regional development.

title: Internet Paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: The internet connects millions of devices and enables people to share information across great distances. At home or school, a learner can search for explanations, read digital books, watch a lesson, submit work, or speak with a teacher.
plainContent: The Internet The internet connects millions of devices and enables people to share information across great distances. At home or school, a learner can search for explanations, read digital books, watch a lesson, submit work, or speak with a teacher. Families use it for communication, shopping, banking, entertainment, and work. Users must remember that not everything online is true or safe. We should compare reliable sources, use strong passwords, keep accounts private, and never harass another person. Spending too much time online can also damage sleep and study habits. A balanced routine and thoughtful behavior make the internet beneficial. It should support education and real relationships rather than replace careful thinking or direct human contact.

title: Our National Flag Paragraph for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: A national flag gives a country a visible sign of identity and independence. Bangladesh’s flag is a green rectangle carrying a red circle slightly toward the hoist.
plainContent: Our National Flag A national flag gives a country a visible sign of identity and independence. Bangladesh’s flag is a green rectangle carrying a red circle slightly toward the hoist. The green recalls the country’s fertile land and lively natural landscape. The red suggests the rising sun as well as the sacrifice made during the struggle for freedom. The flag was designed by artist Kamrul Hassan in its present form. An earlier wartime design included a map of Bangladesh, but the map was later removed so that the flag would remain clear and easy to reproduce. The first version was raised publicly at the University of Dhaka on 2 March 1971, before independence was achieved. The proportions of the flag are 10 units in length to 6 units in width. It is flown on Independence Day, Victory Day, national ceremonies, schools, government buildings, and international occasions. Students should handle it carefully, keep it clean, and never allow it to touch the ground. Respect for the flag is respect for the people and history it represents.

title: Importance of Female Education Paragraph
excerpt: Girls need education for the same reasons boys do: learning develops knowledge, confidence, practical skills, and the ability to make sound decisions.
plainContent: Why every girl deserves schooling Girls need education for the same reasons boys do: learning develops knowledge, confidence, practical skills, and the ability to make sound decisions. An educated woman can care for her health, earn a living, understand her rights, and contribute to family and national development. Keeping girls in school also benefits future generations. Mothers who have received education are more likely to value vaccination, nutrition, and schooling for their children. Yet poverty, unsafe travel, early marriage, and social prejudice still prevent many girls from continuing their studies. Families, schools, and government should work together to remove these obstacles. Supporting female education creates opportunity, reduces inequality, and strengthens society.

title: Environment Pollution Paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: Air, water, and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic, and other waste are released carelessly. Polluted surroundings can cause illness, kill fish and plants, reduce soil fertility, and make cities uncomfortable to live in.
plainContent: Keeping the environment clean Air, water, and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic, and other waste are released carelessly. Polluted surroundings can cause illness, kill fish and plants, reduce soil fertility, and make cities uncomfortable to live in. Factories and vehicles should use cleaner methods, and authorities must collect waste and treat sewage properly. Citizens also have responsibilities: they should use bins, reduce plastic, save water and electricity, plant trees, and avoid burning rubbish. Environmental protection is not an occasional campaign. It is a daily practice shared by households, schools, businesses, and government. Clean surroundings support healthy lives and a safer future.

title: Mobile Phone paragraph
excerpt: A mobile phone is a portable device used for calls, messages, photography, internet access, navigation, learning, and emergency assistance. Students can use educational applications, dictionaries, recorded lessons, and online libraries.
plainContent: Mobile Phone A mobile phone is a portable device used for calls, messages, photography, internet access, navigation, learning, and emergency assistance. Students can use educational applications, dictionaries, recorded lessons, and online libraries. Families can remain connected even when members live in different places. The device becomes harmful when it controls the user. Excessive gaming and social media can reduce sleep, attention, physical activity, and face-to-face conversation. Distracted driving, unsafe sharing of photographs, scams, and cyberbullying are additional risks. We should keep phones away during study and meals, protect personal information, and follow school and road rules. A phone is useful equipment when guided by self-control.

title: Road Accident Paragraph
excerpt: A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, or roadside objects. It may occur on a highway, street, bridge, or village road.
plainContent: Road Accidents A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, or roadside objects. It may occur on a highway, street, bridge, or village road. Speeding, reckless overtaking, driving while tired, using a phone, ignoring signals, and driving an unfit vehicle are common causes. Poor lighting, damaged roads, untrained drivers, and careless pedestrians add to the danger. Accidents cause death, injury, disability, emotional pain, and financial loss. A single crash can affect an entire family and delay traffic for thousands of people. Safety begins with behaviour: drivers should obey speed limits, wear seat belts or helmets, avoid alcohol and phones, and never drive when exhausted. Pedestrians should use footpaths and crossings where available and look carefully before crossing. Authorities must enforce licensing rules, inspect vehicles, repair roads, improve signs and lighting, and educate the public. Emergency services should be able to reach crash sites quickly. Road safety is a shared responsibility. Patience and respect for traffic rules can save lives that no later punishment can restore.

title: Dialogue How to Make a Good Result
excerpt: Building strong study habits: Kamal opens the conversation by asking, “Examinations are approaching, and I do not know how to organize my preparation.” Jamal responds, “Begin with a realistic timetable.
plainContent: Building strong study habits Kamal: Examinations are approaching, and I do not know how to organize my preparation. Jamal: Begin with a realistic timetable. List every subject, identify weak chapters, and assign short study periods with breaks. Kamal: I usually read the textbook repeatedly but forget it during the test. Jamal: Close the book and recall the main points. Solve practice questions, explain a lesson aloud, and review mistakes rather than merely rereading. Kamal: Should I study all night? Jamal: No. Adequate sleep, nutritious food, exercise, and a calm mind improve memory. Keep your phone away during focused study and ask teachers about difficult topics. Kamal: I also lose marks because I rush. Jamal: Practise writing within a time limit. In the examination, read directions carefully, plan long answers, and leave a few minutes for checking. Kamal: I will start today and measure progress by completed tasks, not by hours spent at the desk. Jamal: That is a sensible approach. Consistent effort usually produces better results than last-minute pressure.

title: Advantage & Disadvantage of Village life and City life Dialogue
excerpt: Comparing rural and urban living: Rasel opens the conversation by asking, “Would you prefer to live in a village or a city?” Mita responds, “I enjoy village life because it is quieter, greener, and closer to fields and open water.
plainContent: Comparing rural and urban living Rasel: Would you prefer to live in a village or a city? Mita: I enjoy village life because it is quieter, greener, and closer to fields and open water. Neighbours often know one another and help during difficulties. Rasel: Cities offer more colleges, hospitals, jobs, libraries, and cultural events. Public transport and internet services may also be easier to find. Mita: That is true, but cities can be crowded, noisy, polluted, and expensive. Villages may have limited specialist healthcare, employment, and reliable transport. Rasel: Rural areas are changing too. Better roads, schools, and digital connections can provide opportunities without destroying their peaceful character. Mita: And cities can learn from villages by protecting open spaces, reducing pollution, and encouraging community relationships. Rasel: Neither way of life is perfect. The right choice depends on a person’s work, family, and needs. Mita: Improving both places is more useful than arguing that one is always superior.

title: Discipline Composition
excerpt: Discipline is the habit of following sensible rules and completing duties at the proper time. It does not mean blind punishment; it means controlling impulses so that an important goal is not lost to temporary comfort.
plainContent: Discipline as a guide to life Discipline is the habit of following sensible rules and completing duties at the proper time. It does not mean blind punishment; it means controlling impulses so that an important goal is not lost to temporary comfort. A disciplined student attends lessons, keeps materials organized, studies regularly, respects others, and submits work honestly. A disciplined worker arrives on time and completes responsibilities carefully. In public life, obeying traffic rules, keeping promises, and protecting shared spaces are also forms of discipline. Without discipline, talent remains unreliable. A person may have intelligence but fail because of laziness, poor time management, or uncontrolled habits. Discipline turns small daily efforts into skill and achievement. It also builds self-respect because people learn that they can depend on their own decisions. Good routines should be realistic. Time for sleep, recreation, family, and rest prevents discipline from becoming unhealthy pressure. With patience and repeated practice, orderly habits make both personal and social life more successful.

title: Student life Composition for Class 5, 6, 7, 8, SSC – Easy
excerpt: Student life is the period when a person builds knowledge, habits, character, and plans for the future. It is not only a time for passing examinations.
plainContent: Student Life Student life is the period when a person builds knowledge, habits, character, and plans for the future. It is not only a time for passing examinations. A student learns in classrooms, libraries, laboratories, playgrounds, families, and communities. The first duty of a student is sincere study. Regular attendance, careful reading, practice, and questions help turn information into understanding. Students should manage time, keep healthy routines, respect teachers, cooperate with classmates, and take part in useful cultural or sporting activities. Service projects can teach empathy and responsibility. Student life also has challenges. Competition, distraction, fear of failure, and pressure from others can cause stress. A balanced routine, honest communication, sufficient sleep, and asking for help can make these difficulties manageable. Success should be measured by progress and integrity, not only by marks. The habits formed during these years influence adult life. A disciplined, curious, kind, and adaptable learner can become a capable citizen. Therefore students should use their opportunities wisely and prepare themselves not just for employment, but for responsible participation in society.

title: Value of Time Composition for Class 6,7,8,SSC,HSC
excerpt: Time is the portion of life in which every goal must be pursued. Money can sometimes be earned again and health may be restored with care, but a moment that has passed cannot be bought back.
plainContent: The Value of Time Time is the portion of life in which every goal must be pursued. Money can sometimes be earned again and health may be restored with care, but a moment that has passed cannot be bought back. For that reason, wise people treat time as a resource more precious than possessions. Using time well does not mean working without rest. It means choosing priorities, beginning tasks promptly, and giving study, work, family, health, and relaxation their proper places. A student can divide a large assignment into daily steps and review progress each evening. A worker can prepare a short list and avoid unnecessary delays. Wasted hours often disappear through idleness, endless scrolling, or postponing difficult duties. Procrastination creates stress because unfinished work remains in the mind. Punctuality also shows respect for other people’s time and builds trust. We should set realistic goals, keep a routine, and adapt when unexpected events occur. Small useful actions repeated every day produce large results. When we value time, we make better use of education and opportunity and reduce regret about the past.

title: Dengue Fever paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: Dengue is a viral illness spread mainly by infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes often breed in small amounts of water collected in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters, or uncovered tanks.
plainContent: Dengue fever and prevention Dengue is a viral illness spread mainly by infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes often breed in small amounts of water collected in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters, or uncovered tanks. A patient may develop sudden fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea, or a rash. Anyone with these symptoms should contact a qualified health professional, especially if the fever is high or persistent. Bleeding, repeated vomiting, abdominal pain, unusual sleepiness, or difficulty breathing are warning signs that require urgent care. Self-medication can be risky, so advice from a doctor is important. Families can reduce risk by emptying containers, cleaning drains, covering stored water, wearing protective clothing, and using approved mosquito protection. Schools and local authorities should keep public areas clean and spread accurate information. Community action is the strongest defence against dengue.

title: Newspaper Composition
excerpt: A newspaper is a regular publication that reports events and presents comment on matters of public interest. It may appear in print, on a website, or through a digital app.
plainContent: Newspaper A newspaper is a regular publication that reports events and presents comment on matters of public interest. It may appear in print, on a website, or through a digital app. Its pages commonly include national and international news, education, science, health, business, sports, culture, weather, and classified notices. Newspapers connect citizens with the country and the wider world. A student who reads one regularly learns new words, discovers useful facts, and develops ideas for essays and discussions. Reports about public decisions can also help people understand their rights and responsibilities. Editorials and columns encourage readers to think about problems from different perspectives. A newspaper must be read thoughtfully. A responsible reader checks the source, notices the date, and does not share an unverified claim simply because its headline is exciting. News and opinion should not be confused. Printed papers remain useful, while digital editions make information faster to access. Newspapers can influence society by exposing wrongdoing, highlighting neglected communities, and encouraging constructive debate. Their value is greatest when journalists work honestly and readers remain critical. Therefore, regular newspaper reading is a simple way to become informed, improve language skill, and participate wisely in civic life.

title: Aim in Life Composition
excerpt: A person’s aim in life is a clear idea about the kind of work and contribution he or she hopes to make. Without a direction, time and talent can easily be wasted.
plainContent: Choosing a direction A person’s aim in life is a clear idea about the kind of work and contribution he or she hopes to make. Without a direction, time and talent can easily be wasted. My present aim is to become a teacher who makes learning accessible to children in both towns and villages. I have chosen this goal because education changes the opportunities available to families. A capable teacher can explain lessons, encourage shy learners, and help students develop honesty, discipline, and independent judgment. To prepare, I must study regularly, improve my communication skills, read widely, and learn how to use modern teaching tools. Patience and empathy are as important as examination results. An aim should guide daily habits rather than remain an attractive sentence. I will review my progress, correct weaknesses, and seek advice from experienced people. Whatever profession a person chooses, success is most meaningful when personal achievement is joined with useful service to society.

title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin Completing Story
excerpt: The town of Hamelin was overrun by rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people.
plainContent: The Pied Piper of Hamelin The town of Hamelin was overrun by rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people. The mayor promised a large reward to anyone who could rid the town of the pests. A travelling piper arrived and said that his music could lead the rats away. He played a strange, bright tune, and every rat followed him through the streets and out to the river. He guided them safely away, then returned to claim the promised payment. The mayor had expected the piper to work for less and refused to pay the full reward. The piper warned him that a promise made publicly must be honoured, but the mayor dismissed him. The piper then played another tune. This time the town’s children followed him beyond the gates. When the mayor and citizens realised what was happening, they begged him to return them. The piper brought the children back only after the town paid what it had promised and apologised. From then on, Hamelin’s leaders kept their word. Moral: A promise is a responsibility, not an opportunity for dishonest bargaining.

title: Dialogue Bad Effect of Smoking
excerpt: A warning about tobacco: Rafi opens the conversation by asking, “My older cousin has started smoking because he thinks it makes him look mature.” Joya responds, “Tobacco does not prove maturity.
plainContent: A warning about tobacco Rafi: My older cousin has started smoking because he thinks it makes him look mature. Joya: Tobacco does not prove maturity. It contains addictive substances and exposes the body to harmful chemicals. Rafi: What damage can it cause? Joya: It raises the risk of lung disease, heart problems, stroke, and several cancers. Smoke also harms people nearby, especially children. Money spent on cigarettes could support food, books, or savings. Rafi: Some people say they can stop whenever they wish. Joya: Dependence makes quitting difficult, but support from a doctor, family, or cessation programme can help. Avoiding triggers and replacing the habit with exercise or another activity is useful. Rafi: We should not tease someone who is trying to quit. Joya: Right. Encouragement is more helpful than shame. Young people should learn the facts before advertising or peer pressure influences them. Rafi: I will share reliable health information with my cousin and ask whether he wants help.

title: Food Adulteration paragraph for Class 6,7,8, HSC, SSC
excerpt: Food adulteration occurs when sellers mix inferior, contaminated, or harmful substances into food or use unsafe chemicals to make it look better or last longer. Milk, spices, oil, fruit, fish, sweets, and packaged products can all be affected.
plainContent: The danger of adulterated food Food adulteration occurs when sellers mix inferior, contaminated, or harmful substances into food or use unsafe chemicals to make it look better or last longer. Milk, spices, oil, fruit, fish, sweets, and packaged products can all be affected. Eating such food may cause immediate stomach problems and can damage organs after repeated exposure. Children, older people, and those with weak health face particular risks. Adulteration is therefore not a minor business offence; it threatens public health. Consumers should buy from reliable sources, inspect packaging, check dates, wash produce, and be cautious about unnatural colours or unusually low prices. Authorities must test food, inspect businesses, punish offenders, and educate the public. Honest sellers and informed buyers can help create a safer food market.

title: Drug Addiction Paragraph for Class 6-12, SSC, HSC
excerpt: Drug addiction begins when repeated use of a substance changes a person’s body and behaviour. What starts as curiosity or pressure from friends can become dependence.
plainContent: Protecting young people from drugs Drug addiction begins when repeated use of a substance changes a person’s body and behaviour. What starts as curiosity or pressure from friends can become dependence. An addicted person may lose interest in study, work, health, and family responsibilities. The effects include illness, financial hardship, broken relationships, accidents, and crime. A family should not hide the problem or wait until it becomes severe. Doctors, counsellors, and treatment centres can provide safer and more effective help. Education, sports, creative activities, caring relationships, and honest conversations can prevent many young people from experimenting. Authorities must stop illegal trafficking while making treatment available to those who need it. We should reject drugs firmly but treat affected people with humanity so that they can seek recovery.

title: A Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed Completing story for all classes
excerpt: Two travellers were walking through a forest when they heard a bear approaching. One man quickly climbed a tree and left his companion on the ground.
plainContent: Tested beside the forest path Two travellers were walking through a forest when they heard a bear approaching. One man quickly climbed a tree and left his companion on the ground. The other remembered that a bear is unlikely to touch a person who appears lifeless, so he held his breath and remained still. The bear came close, examined him, and then moved away. When the danger had passed, the man in the tree climbed down and jokingly asked what the bear had whispered. His companion replied that the animal had advised him never to trust a person who abandons a friend in danger. The words were calm, but the lesson was serious. Friendship is not measured by cheerful conversations or shared meals. It is revealed when help is inconvenient and fear is real. A dependable friend offers support instead of searching for personal safety first. Moral: A true friend stands beside us during difficulty.

title: Computer Paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: Computers help people complete many tasks accurately and quickly. A learner can type an assignment, organize information, calculate expenses, draw a chart, or attend an online class with the same device.
plainContent: The value of learning computer skills Computers help people complete many tasks accurately and quickly. A learner can type an assignment, organize information, calculate expenses, draw a chart, or attend an online class with the same device. Offices, hospitals, banks, shops, and schools all depend on computer-based work. Knowing how to use a computer also broadens access to knowledge. Students can consult digital libraries and practise languages, while job seekers can prepare applications and develop professional skills. However, users must learn online safety as well as technical operations. Strong passwords, careful downloads, privacy settings, and balanced screen time are essential. Computer education should be practical and available to everyone. A person who understands the basics can adapt to new software and work more confidently. Used wisely, a computer saves time, encourages creativity, and connects people with useful opportunities.

title: Traffic Jam Paragraph for class 6,7,8, SSC
excerpt: A traffic jam is a long queue of vehicles moving slowly or not at all. It is common in crowded cities where the number of cars, buses, trucks, rickshaws, and motorcycles has grown faster than the roads and transport systems.
plainContent: Traffic Jam A traffic jam is a long queue of vehicles moving slowly or not at all. It is common in crowded cities where the number of cars, buses, trucks, rickshaws, and motorcycles has grown faster than the roads and transport systems. Narrow streets, road repairs, illegal parking, roadside markets, poor signals, and careless driving make congestion worse. A jam wastes valuable time and fuel. Students may miss classes, workers arrive late, and patients can face dangerous delays. Exhaust fumes increase air pollution, while constant horns create stress and noise. Goods also reach shops more slowly, raising business costs. Better public transport can reduce the number of private vehicles. Authorities should improve traffic signals, create safe footpaths and parking areas, remove illegal obstructions, and enforce lane and stopping rules. Traffic police need effective training and equipment. Citizens should plan journeys, avoid blocking intersections, and follow directions patiently. Long-term city planning that places homes, workplaces, and services near reliable transport is essential. Cooperation between planners, drivers, pedestrians, and businesses can make urban travel safer and faster.

title: A Thirsty Crow completing story For Class 6,7,8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: On a hot day a crow searched for water and found a narrow jar. A little water lay at the bottom, but the bird’s beak could not reach it.
plainContent: Resourcefulness beside the jar On a hot day a crow searched for water and found a narrow jar. A little water lay at the bottom, but the bird’s beak could not reach it. It tried to tip the jar, yet the vessel was too heavy. It also searched around the yard for another source and found none. Instead of giving up, the crow noticed small pebbles nearby. It carried them to the jar one by one and dropped them inside. Slowly the water rose until it reached the rim. The crow drank safely and flew away. The solution was not quick, but patient observation turned a difficult problem into a manageable task. When the first plan fails, a person can examine the materials at hand, think step by step, and continue working rather than complain. Moral: Intelligence, patience, and perseverance can overcome obstacles.

It supports the three main HSC groups: Science Business Studies Humanities The calculator also supports the 4th or optional subject , allowing the applicable bonus to be included automatically. If you already have your marks or grades, enter them above to get your estimated HSC GPA. How to Calculate HSC GPA Bangladesh's HSC grading system uses a 5.00-point scale . Each subject result is converted into a letter grade and corresponding grade point. For example: 80–100 marks = A+ = 5.00 70–79 marks = A = 4.00 60–69 marks = A− = 3.50 50–59 marks = B = 3.00 40–49 marks = C = 2.00 33–39 marks = D = 1.00 0–32 marks = F = 0.00 The official Education Board grading table uses this marks-to-grade-point scale. For the main subjects, the grade points are used to determine the student's GPA. If an optional or 4th subject is included, the applicable bonus is added according to the grading rules. Simple example Suppose a student receives these grade points: Subject Grade Grade Point Bangla A+ 5.00 English A 4.00 ICT A+ 5.00 Physics A+ 5.00 Chemistry A 4.00 Biology A+ 5.00 The grade points from the main subjects are used to calculate the student's GPA. If the student also has an optional subject, the 4th-subject rule is applied before the final GPA is determined. HSC Grading System in Bangladesh The HSC grading system uses a 5.00 GPA scale. The following table shows the standard marks-to-grade conversion used by Bangladesh's Education Boards. Marks Letter Grade Grade Point 80–100 A+ 5.00 70–79 A 4.00 60–69 A− 3.50 50–59 B 3.00 40–49 C 2.00 33–39 D 1.00 0–32 F 0.00 What do the grades mean? A+ (5.00) The highest grade point on the HSC grading scale. A (4.00) A strong result with a grade point of 4.00. A− (3.50) A grade point of 3.50. B (3.00) A grade point of 3.00. C (2.00) A grade point of 2.00. D (1.00) The minimum passing grade. F (0.00) A failing grade in the subject. HSC 4th Subject Bonus: How Does It Work? The 4th subject, also called the optional subject , is treated differently from the main subjects. When the grade point earned in the optional subject is above 2.00 , the amount above 2.00 is treated as the bonus. For example: Optional subject grade point = 5.00 Then: 5.00 − 2.00 = 3.00 bonus points Similarly: Optional subject grade point = 4.00 4.00 − 2.00 = 2.00 bonus points And: Optional subject grade point = 3.50 3.50 − 2.00 = 1.50 bonus points The bonus is then incorporated into the overall GPA calculation according to the applicable HSC rules. Our calculator applies the 4th-subject calculation automatically, so you do not need to calculate the bonus manually.
